Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

case noun

at law

also lawsuit, legal case, court case

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.199: causam agere (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 1.4.1: causam obtinēre (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 194

causa, causae f.

noun, first declension

a case at law; one’s side in it

causam agere, to plead a case; causam dīcere, to defend oneself; causam obtinēre, to win it; causā cadere, to lose it (Lewis & Short). A civil case is a causa prīvāta, a criminal case a causa pūblica (Traupman 194).

Examples

  • līs ad forum dēducta est, vespā jūdice

    the case went to court, with a wasp as judgePhaedr. 3.13.3

  • grammaticī certant et adhūc sub jūdice līs est

    the scholars are at odds, and the case is still before the judgeHor. Ars 78

  • Estne causa prīvāta an causa pūblica?

    Is it a civil case or a criminal case?Traupman 192

Other words

  • līs, lītis f. — a lawsuit; a dispute

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Hor. Ars 78: adhūc sub jūdice līs est; Phaedr. 3.13.3; Traupman 194–195

    Properly a quarrel, then a quarrel taken to court: lītem alicui intendere, to bring a lawsuit against someone (Cic. de Or. 1.42, Lewis & Short; Traupman 195).

See also law, case.
